A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe the same SimVQ study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendix 8.1–8.4 support reliable comparison; the three appendix pages render identically.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet and LibriTTS reconstruction experiments, codebook ablations, toy simulations, and qualitative results, including appendix figures.

after.justification: v3 retains the original ImageNet and LibriTTS experiments, ablations, toy simulations, and qualitative appendix results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same frozen codebook C, learnable linear basis W, quantization procedure, and training objective. Algorithm 1 and the method in Section 4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet image reconstruction, LibriTTS-580h training with test-clean/test-other evaluation, and the same Gaussian toy scenario. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical comparator membership: VQGAN variants, FSQ, LFQ, and VQGAN-LC-CLIP for images; EnCodec, Vocos, SpeechTokenizer, and WavTokenizer for audio. Ablation and appendix comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix Table 5 retain the same resolutions, audio windows, training budgets, batch sizes, codebook sizes, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Both retain the codebook-size and optimization ablations in Tables 3–4, toy optimization analyses, latent-basis analysis, and appendix loss curves, codebook distributions, and qualitative cases. Their questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. Reporting practices are unchanged; paired audio scores represent test-clean/test-other results.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 1–4 and appendix figures. For example, SimVQ's ImageNet rFID remains 2.24 at 65,536 codes and 1.99 at 262,144 codes in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(18), mathematical definitions, and the optimization and convergence arguments are unchanged. Equation placement changes do not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about disjoint optimization, the one-layer SimVQ solution, codebook utilization, scalability, and applicability to images and audio.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of codebook scaling and latent-basis behavior are unchanged. Section 6 retains the qualification that better reconstruction need not yield better downstream generation.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract statement that code is available and supplies the youngsheen/SimVQ GitHub repository address, absent from v2. This adds access information; implementation details and appendix configurations remain unchanged. Repository availability and contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 44 works and retain the same related-work discussion and research positioning. A changed citation page backlink reflects pagination only.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short code-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, and section hierarchy are unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing text and equations reflow across columns and pages: Equation (11) moves from PDF page 4 to 5, and the conclusion extends onto page 9. Figure and table designs remain unchanged, and all appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer in v3's abstract provides a concrete route to the implementation, modestly improving reproducibility information and resource discoverability. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. The supported benefit is the added access information; the PDFs alone cannot verify the repository's usability.
